quiz.question: What is the most effective approach to handle hot keys in a distributed cache system?
options: Increase the TTL on every key
Replicate hot keys across multiple cache instances
Store hot keys only in the database
Use a single larger cache node
quiz.explanation: Keeping redundant copies of popular posts on several cache instances spreads reads so no single node becomes the bottleneck.

quiz.question: Why do mega accounts (millions of followers) break a pure fan-out-on-write feed?
options: Each post requires writing to millions of precomputed feeds
quiz.explanation: Fanning out to millions of feeds per post is enormous write amplification, which is why hybrid feeds fetch those posts at read time instead.

quiz.question: In a hybrid feed, how are posts from very popular accounts handled?
options: They are merged into the feed at read time
They are written to every follower's feed synchronously
They are only shown to mutual friends
quiz.explanation: Regular accounts are fanned out on write; posts from mega accounts are pulled in and merged when a user reads their feed.

quiz.question: Why can the Post cache use a long TTL with LRU eviction?
options: Caches never run out of memory
quiz.explanation: Posts change rarely, so long TTLs are safe and LRU keeps the most recently read posts in memory.
